requirement:
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:

> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.

Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. This citation is optional;
helpers need no annotation merely because they serve other code.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.util` states only observable behavior, so it has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. I checked each clause for an implementation choice it prescribes.

- **"Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` ... with this text"**: This is about what users see. A built-in table, a generated file, or a hard-coded string would all give the same fixed text and name. The text names no library, type, signature, or interface.
- **"Only `{cite}` MAY reference it"**: This is a validation outcome. It could be enforced in a role check or a per-built-in permitted-roles table, and the visible result is the same. The shared validation rule is already stated in `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`.
- **"An item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review"**: This is the observable validation outcome. It is also stated in `requirements.references.citation_review`.
- **"This citation is optional"**: This is a statement of permission, so it imposes nothing to check.

The subject has no `Implements` edges, and the review roots are empty. That is consistent with there being nothing structural to implement.

behavioral: The tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.references.util`.

1. **Habeas provides `habeas:util` with the stated text.**
   - `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations]` checks that `builtin("habeas:util")` exists and that its text starts and ends with the expected wording.
   - The same test asserts that the text equals the block quoted in `md/reference.md`.
   - `Builtin::text` in `src/builtins.rs` takes the text from the requirement chapter itself with `quoted_text(chapter, ":::{req} util")`. The unit test therefore ties the built-in's text to the requirement text.
   - The same test confirms that unknown names such as `habeas:none` and `habeas:other` do not resolve.

2. **Only `{cite}` may reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary.**
   - The unit test asserts `util.check(Cite)` succeeds and that `{impl}` and `{test}` are rejected with the message "built-in habeas:util may only be referenced with {cite}".
   - `tests/references.rs#fn[habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review]` covers an inline citation (`inline`), a fenced citation with commentary (`fenced`) and a bare fence (`bare`). It asserts that none of them produces an error. It also asserts that validation reports the `{impl}` and `{test}` uses at their lines.
   - `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` covers the fenced form with commentary (`glue`) and an inline reference inside a fence body (`empty`). It also covers a wrong role in a fence.
   - `src/citations.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_commentary_groups_nested_citations_but_excludes_declarations_and_literals]` covers `habeas:util` in book fences.

3. **An item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` needs no citation review.**
   - `habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review` asserts there is no "missing citation review" error for `inline`, `fenced` or `bare`.
   - The same test asserts that `mixed`, which also cites `rules.ready`, still needs a review. This is the case where the item has another citation.
   - `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated` asserts that `empty`, which mixes `habeas:util` with `rules.ready`, still needs a review, and that `glue` does not.

4. **The citation is optional.** This is permissive wording and imposes no behavior to test.

I found no untested obligation and no wrong assertion. Every relevant test already carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.

text: :::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. This citation is optional;
helpers need no annotation merely because they serve other code.
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas provides built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in has fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation,
and states which reference roles may use it. References resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, a
built-in reference displayed under {cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`
uses a badge without a link whose hover text gives the built-in's full text.
Built-ins themselves neither require nor permit definition evidence files and
do not appear as definitions in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of
{cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. Per-source citation reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` may be required for references
to a built-in. A project definition cannot use a full name beginning with
`habeas:`; validation reports one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation reports a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Fenced commentary elsewhere in the book is reviewed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
